title: Preparing to meet Him
hookLine: whoever loves to meet Allah, Allah loves to meet him; and Aisha's honest question
tomorrow: what should be on your mind at the very end?

cards: Before a first date, or meeting someone's parents, there's a ritual. The shower, the clean shirt, a little scent at the wrist, one more look in the mirror. You get ready because the meeting matters.

A hadith in Sahih al-Bukhari answers yesterday's question with a meeting: whoever loves to meet Allah, Allah loves to meet him, and whoever dislikes meeting Allah, Allah dislikes meeting him. Loving the end of the road?
That sounds impossible. Someone in the room said so, out loud.

teach.b: It was Aisha, the wife of the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ. In the report she says, plainly: but we all dislike death.
And he answers: it isn't that. When a believer's time comes, he is given good news of Allah's mercy and pleasure, and then nothing is dearer to him than what lies ahead.
So the hadith doesn't ask anyone to like dying, and Aisha's honest question stays in the record. It's about the meeting, and whether you've been getting ready for someone you love.
In Islam, getting ready often runs through the senses.
Before every prayer, wudu: water on the hands, the mouth, the face. Before Friday prayer, a report in Bukhari mentions washing, cleaning the teeth with a miswak, and wearing scent if you have it.
The body rehearses standing before Allah, again and again. Preparing to meet Him, then, isn't a grim project.
It looks like any meeting with someone you love: wash, put on something clean, think about what you'll say, settle what's unsettled.
Notice the shape of the sentence: the love runs both ways.

how: Muslims prepare for prayer with wudu, and for Friday prayer by washing, cleaning the teeth and wearing scent if they have it; teachers often pair this hadith with the idea that a whole life can be a getting-ready to meet Allah.

games.q: what does “preparing to meet him” mean?
o: keeping your will and funeral plans updated each year
praying extra in the days just before someone dies
getting ready for the meeting with Allah, as for someone loved

games.q: what's inside the hadith — tap the pairs.
p: it isn't that: good news comes at the end
wash, miswak, scent if you have it

s: this hadith asks Muslims to like the idea of dying
Aisha said we all dislike death; he answered: it isn't that. it's about the meeting and the good news at the end.
in the report, Aisha pushes back on the Prophet's words
she says, plainly, that we all dislike death, and her question stays in the record.
a report in Bukhari mentions wearing scent as part of getting ready for Friday prayer
washing, cleaning the teeth, and scent if you have it.

games.q: your uncle admits he dreads death and feels guilty about it, because he's heard 'the believer loves to meet Allah.' what did the Prophet say to the same worry?
o: it isn't about liking death; at the end, the believer gets good news.
real believers never fear death, so he should work on his faith.
the hadith is only about scholars and saints, not ordinary people.
games.why: Aisha raised exactly this: we all dislike death. his answer: it isn't that. at the end comes good news of mercy, and then the meeting is wanted.

practice: If there's soap and water near you, or a little scent, use it now. Wash your hands slowly, or touch a drop of scent to your wrist, and notice the cool of the water or the smell as you breathe.
While you do, name one thing you'd want settled before a meeting that matters: a call you owe, a word you haven't said.

wordCard.voice: Preparing to meet Him: getting ready for the meeting with Allah the way you'd get ready to meet someone you love. Clean, settled, and glad to go.

orig.note: Arabic: meeting Allah; the phrase at the heart of this hadith.

carryVoice: Keep this one close: loves to meet him, a love the hadith says runs both ways. See you tomorrow.

sources.ref: Sahih al-Bukhari 6507 (also Sahih Muslim 2684): whoever loves to meet Allah, Allah loves to meet him; Aisha says we all dislike death; the Prophet answers that at death the believer is given good news of Allah's mercy and pleasure
Sahih al-Bukhari 880: on Friday, washing, cleaning the teeth with a miswak, and using scent if available
